title: Утренний звонок дочери  (A Daughter's Morning Call)

segments.t: Chef Viktor Barinov wakes up startled after another night with young waitress Eva and tries to pretend nothing happened. Before he can even finish his morning coffee, Katya calls his phone and asks him to reject Denis when the young cook comes seeking permission to date her.
Кто здесь? Почему в комнате так тихо?
Доброе утро, мой дорогой Виктор Петрович!
Снова делаете вид, что меня здесь нет?
Это вполне в вашем обычном стиле.
Подожди тихо, мне звонит старшая дочь.
Алло, Катя, о чём ты говоришь?
Папа, к тебе сегодня зайдёт повар Денис.
Он спросит разрешения встречаться со мной.
Ты можешь сразу строго его отшить?
Ну конечно, дочка, могла даже не просить!
Я с большим удовольствием прогоню этого парня!
Большое спасибо, папа, ты меня спас!
Let's examine Chef Barinov's awkward morning with Eva and Katya's phone call.
Кто здесь? Почему в комнате так тихо?

'Who is here? Why is it so quiet in the room?' Here wondering who here is shows Barinov looking for the real truth. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Доброе утро, мой дорогой Виктор Петрович!
'Good morning, my dear Viktor Petrovich!' Around the date and moment, Eva makes her point loud and clear.
Снова делаете вид, что меня здесь нет?

'Are you pretending again that I am not here?' Checking whether Barinov pretending again that she is not here cuts straight through the tension between Eva and Barinov. In Russian, she does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Это вполне в вашем обычном стиле.

'That is completely in your usual style.' Admitting that that is completely in Barinov's usual style shows Eva being honest for a change. Russian drops "is" in the present, setting the two halves of the thought side by side.
Подожди тихо, мне звонит старшая дочь.
'Wait quietly, my eldest daughter is calling me.' Saying that quietly his eldest daughter is calling him is how Barinov sets the tone with Eva.
Алло, Катя, о чём ты говоришь?

'Hello, Katya, what are you talking about?' By wondering what Eva talking is, Barinov presses Eva for a straight answer. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.
Папа, к тебе сегодня зайдёт повар Денис.

'Dad, the cook Denis will drop by to see you today.' Adding that dad the cook Denis will drop by to see Barinov today fills in the missing piece for Barinov. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
Он спросит разрешения встречаться со мной.
'He will ask permission to go out with me.' Saying that he will ask permission to go out is how Katya sets the tone with Barinov.
Ты можешь сразу строго его отшить?

'Can you brush him off strictly right away?' Here checking whether Barinov brush him off strictly right away shows Katya looking for the real truth. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
Ну конечно, дочка, могла даже не просить!

'Well of course, daughter, you did not even have to ask!' Insisting that daughter Eva did not even have to ask shows Barinov is not backing down. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat.
Я с большим удовольствием прогоню этого парня!
'I will chase this guy away with great pleasure!' Once he will chase this guy away with great pleasure, Barinov makes sure Eva hears every word.
Большое спасибо, папа, ты меня спас!

'Thank you very much, Dad, you saved me!' With the moment and morning at stake, Katya reacts without holding back. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is. Now listen to the complete morning scene with Chef Barinov, Eva, and Katya.

Happy to turn down any suitor chasing his daughter, Chef Barinov heads to his restaurant office—where Lyova is waiting with a delicate request. Until next time!
До свидания!
